components.name: Window Chrome
components.description: Shared header/body chrome for every content window (About, Projects, Tools, Activity, Milestones, Contact).
components.html:
About Me — Resume.txt
Window content goes here.
components.css: .ds-window { border: 0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.12); border-radius: 12px; box-shadow: 0 24px 70px rgba(15,20,35,0.32), 0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.08); overflow: hidden; background: #fbfbfd; color: #1d1d1f; } .ds-window-header { height: 40px; display: flex; align-items: center; padding: 0 14px; border-bottom: 0.5px solid rgba(0,0,0,0.09); background: #f2f2f4; } .ds-dots { display: flex; gap: 8px; } .ds-dot { width: 12px; height: 12px; border-radius: 50%; } .ds-dot-close { background: #ff5f57; cursor: pointer; } .ds-dot-min { background: #febc2e; } .ds-dot-zoom { background: #28c840; } .ds-window-title { flex: 1; text-align: center; font-size: 13px; font-weight: 600; margin-right: 52px; color: #86868b; } .ds-window-body { padding: 30px 34px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.65; }

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The single accent-filled action per screen (Email me, View Live).
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 16px; background: #0a84ff; color: #fff; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #0972dd; } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0a84ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Neutral secondary action (Source, GitHub, LinkedIn links).
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-size: 13px; font-weight: 500; padding: 8px 16px; background: #eef0f3; color: #3a3a3f; border: none; border-radius: 8px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { background: #e4e6ea; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #0a84ff; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Neutral Chip
components.description: Skill / tool tags inside About and Tools windows.
components.css: .ds-chip { font-size: 13px; padding: 5px 12px; border-radius: 8px; background: #eef0f3; color: #3a3a3f; display: inline-block; }

components.name: Accent Chip
components.description: Project-detail tags — the one place chips take the accent color.
components.css: .ds-chip-accent { font-size: 12px; padding: 4px 10px; background: rgba(10,132,255,0.14); color: #0a84ff; border-radius: 7px; font-weight: 500; display: inline-block; }

components.name: Dock
components.description: Fixed-bottom frosted-glass icon dock; the primary navigation between windows.
components.css: .ds-dock { display: flex; align-items: flex-end; gap: 12px; padding: 10px 14px; backdrop-filter: saturate(180%) blur(24px); border: 0.5px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.6); border-radius: 22px; box-shadow: 0 12px 40px rgba(15,20,35,0.28); background: rgba(255,255,255,0.5); } .ds-dock-icon { width: 52px; height: 52px; border-radius: 13px; box-shadow: 0 4px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.2); transition: transform 0.16s ease; cursor: pointer; } .ds-dock-icon:hover { transform: translateY(-10px) scale(1.12); } .ds-dock-divider { width: 0.5px; height: 42px; margin: 0 1px; background: rgba(0,0,0,0.14); }

narrative.overview: MeetMe recreates the feeling of opening someone's actual Mac and finding their work already open in front of you — windows scattered mid-thought, a dock along the bottom, a Spotlight search a keystroke away. It is not a portfolio about a desktop; it behaves like one: windows drag, stack, focus, and close with the same physics macOS trained everyone to expect. That familiarity is the trick — because the interaction model is free, every ounce of personality gets to live in the details instead: the equalizer bars on 'Now Playing,' the forecast-styled career milestones, the Finder-style project browser. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS-portfolio look: no card grids of identical project tiles, no gradient-text name in a hero, no hero-metric block with big numbers and small labels. It also rejects anything that reads as a resume PDF reformatted for the web — static, list-shaped, skimmed once and forgotten. The desktop metaphor exists so a visitor plays first and reads second.
keyCharacteristics: Native macOS window chrome (traffic-light buttons, 40-44px header bar) on every panel, light or dark.
One accent color (#0a84ff) doing all the signaling work — links, tags, active states — everywhere else stays neutral.
Frosted-glass surfaces reserved for floating, always-on-top chrome: the dock, Spotlight, the theme toggle. Window bodies stay opaque.
Every window pops in with the same winpop micro-animation; nothing on the page enters silently.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue is the only saturated color allowed outside decorative dock-icon gradients and the Now Playing/Milestones widget backgrounds (themed set-pieces, not core palette). If a new element needs to stand out, reach for weight or size before reaching for a second color.

rules.name: The System-Font Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a second typeface family. Every new hierarchy level is built from this one stack via weight, size, and letter-spacing only.

rules.name: The Glass-Is-Chrome-Only Rule
rules.body: Frosted blur is reserved for the dock, Spotlight, and the theme toggle — UI that floats above all windows. Window bodies are always opaque cards, never glass.

dos: Do keep every window's chrome identical (traffic-light dots, header height, 12px radius, the two-part Window shadow).
Do let Signal Blue (#0a84ff) be the only color that means 'interactive' — links, active states, primary buttons, project tags.
Do reserve backdrop-filter blur for floating OS chrome only (dock, Spotlight, theme toggle) per the Glass-Is-Chrome-Only Rule.
Do drive every visual difference between light and dark mode from the shared theme token object — never hardcode a color that isn't accent blue or an intentionally-dark widget.
Do give every window entrance the same winpop pop-in animation, and provide a prefers-reduced-motion fallback for it, the dock hover pop, the equalizer bars, and Spotlight's spotpop.
donts: Don't build a generic 'SaaS portfolio' card grid of identically-sized project tiles with icon + heading + text.
Don't use gradient text (background-clip: text + gradient) anywhere, including on 'MeetMe'.
Don't add a hero-metric block (big number + small label + supporting stats).
Don't make a content window's body translucent/glass — glass is chrome-only.
Don't introduce a second typeface family for any reason.
Don't use border-left/border-right heavier than 1px as a colored accent stripe on any card, chip, or list item.
Don't add a second saturated accent color competing with Signal Blue outside the intentionally-themed dock-icon gradients and Now Playing/Milestones widgets.
